catalogue_metadata.scope_notes: Extraction focused on continuous architecture steering, multi-agent governance, compliance validation, and LLM orchestration within the cas_runner framework.
analysis_limits: Repository inspected without live LLM provider endpoint credentials
Analysis constrained to committed Python sources, configuration manifests, and architecture specifications

system_map.overview: CAS (Continuous Architecture System) provides an agentic runtime that orchestrates software architecture compliance, steering context projection, and automated knowledge evolution. It leverages deterministic flow execution combined with LLM-backed decision synthesis and Git-backed persistent state.

agents.name: FlowRunner
agents.role: Orchestrates multi-step agentic execution flows, manages execution context, and invokes governance and steering tasks.

agents.name: AgenticMerger
agents.role: Resolves architectural intent conflicts and merges multi-project capability records and decisions using structured LLM synthesis.

agents.name: ComplianceEngine
agents.role: Evaluates architectural deltas against defined governance rules and generates structured compliance findings.

agents.name: GovernanceActionEngine
agents.role: Executes state machine transitions across governance artifacts based on compliance findings and promotion decisions.

orchestration.description: FlowRunner manages a centralized pipeline of architectural steps, sequentially evaluating Git deltas, generating prompt facts, dispatching LLM calls via LiteLLM, and persisting state changes to git-backed markdown and YAML files.

tools_and_integrations.name: LiteLLMClient
tools_and_integrations.purpose: Provides unified access to underlying LLM model providers with fallback and parameter management.

tools_and_integrations.name: OpenTelemetry Instrumentation
tools_and_integrations.purpose: Emits distributed execution traces and performance metrics across agentic workflow steps.

tools_and_integrations.name: Git Delta Engine
tools_and_integrations.purpose: Parses repository diffs into structured delta models to ground agent decisions.

state_and_memory.description: Hierarchical Git-backed markdown and YAML repository tracking global and project-level architectural decisions, rules, patterns, and capability records.
Runtime execution profiles, rule contexts, and tracing metrics evaluated dynamically per execution run.
Computed steering projection indices and health scores derived from governance inventory and compliance analysis.

patterns.name: Provider-Agnostic LLM Adapter

tool_protocols.notes: Abstracts underlying LLM calls via litellm unified client interface.

optimisation_targets.notes: Decouples business logic from specific LLM providers and supports test doubles.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Direct wrapper pattern avoiding proprietary vendor lock-in.

patterns.summary: Encapsulates disparate model endpoints behind a uniform interface supporting production and mock execution modes.
patterns.intent: Decouple architectural inference steps from concrete model providers to facilitate testing and multi-model flexibility.
patterns.context: Used across cas_runner whenever agent reasoning, delta evaluation, or text merging is required.
forces: Need to test agent logic deterministically without API costs or network flakiness
Need to route requests across diverse cloud LLM vendors
patterns.solution: Define concrete adapters `LiteLLMClient` and `MockLLMClient` that share call signatures for prompt submission and token management.
implementation_signals: Co-existence of LiteLLMClient and MockLLMClient in src/cas_runner/llm/
Parameterization of client instances into runners and merger components

evidence.note: Production LLM integration wrapping litellm library
Deterministic test double for agent logic verification

benefits: Isolated testing of multi-step agent flows without LLM latency or cost
Seamless swapping of foundation models across execution profiles
costs: Lowest-common-denominator feature exposure across varying provider endpoints
failure_modes: Discrepancies in output formatting between MockLLM responses and real LLM completions

patterns.reuse_notes: Extract `src/cas_runner/llm/` into shared runtime libraries for any multi-agent platform needing mockable LLM IO.

patterns.name: Grounded Prompt Fact Projection

tool_protocols.notes: Compiles facts from Git and models into static prompt context.

optimisation_targets.notes: Reduces hallucination by grounding agent generation strictly in pre-extracted architectural facts.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: System deterministic code projects raw state into explicit prompt facts before agent reasoning.

patterns.summary: Extracts validated facts from code changes and architectural registers to project a deterministic factual basis into agent prompts.
patterns.intent: Prevent LLM hallucinations during governance checks by strictly grounding reasoning on verified capability diffs and historical rules.
patterns.context: Invoked during steering runtime indexing and prompt preparation for architectural decision agents.
forces: Full repository context exceeds LLM prompt token windows and introduces irrelevant noise
Raw Git diffs lack architectural semantic context
patterns.solution: Transform `RawGitDelta` and `CapabilitySet` models into typed `PromptFact` objects collected in a `SteeringRuntimeIndex` prior to agent invocation.
implementation_signals: Typed data structures for PromptFact and SteeringRuntimeIndex in steering models

evidence.note: Defines typed prompt facts and index schema grounding LLM prompts
CI workflow triggering projection generation

benefits: High fidelity of agent decisions directly tied to audited facts
Deterministic traceability of prompt context back to Git commits
costs: Preprocessing overhead required to compile facts before agent activation
failure_modes: Relevant context omissions if fact extraction heuristics miss unconventional architectural changes

patterns.reuse_notes: Adapt `PromptFact` schema for code generation or auditing agents where diffs must be translated to semantic facts.

patterns.name: Agentic Semantic Merge Resolution

tool_protocols.notes: Direct LLM reasoning over conflicting architectural representations.

optimisation_targets.notes: Solves multi-source architectural drift without human triage overhead.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Delegates reconciliation of competing architectural drafts to an LLM agent bounded by schemas.

patterns.summary: Uses an LLM agent to semantically reconcile conflicting architectural documentation and capability records.
patterns.intent: Resolve text-level and conceptual merge conflicts across distributed architectural decisions that standard 3-way git merges fail to handle.
patterns.context: Triggered when multi-project governance blocks or decision templates receive concurrent modifications.
forces: Standard git merges fail on conceptual semantic overlaps in prose and yaml
Manual reconciliation slows down continuous delivery cycles
patterns.solution: Pass conflicting revisions and their lineage to `AgenticMerger`, which prompts an LLM to generate a synthesized `ResolutionResult` conforming to the architectural schema.
implementation_signals: ResolutionResult model capturing merged output and confidence signals

evidence.note: Reconciles governance blocks and models
Structured output model capturing merge resolution outcomes

benefits: Preserves intent across disparate team decisions without human intervention
Generates structured resolution explanations for auditability
costs: Risk of silent semantic degradation if agent misinterprets subtle constraints
failure_modes: LLM hallucinating novel architectural constraints not present in either conflicting source

patterns.reuse_notes: Use this pattern when maintaining central policy documents derived from decentralized project repositories.

patterns.name: State-Machine-Constrained Action Engine

tool_protocols.notes: State transitions are verified deterministically by TransitionRegistry.

optimisation_targets.notes: Prevents unauthorized or out-of-order lifecycle state mutations.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Deterministic guardrails constrain all autonomous state updates.

patterns.summary: Restricts agent-driven governance actions to strictly valid transitions registered in a deterministic state registry.
patterns.intent: Prevent LLM or workflow agents from transitioning architectural assets into invalid lifecycle states (e.g. promoting directly from exploring to stable).
patterns.context: Governs promotions, deprecations, and exceptions across patterns, decisions, and capabilities.
forces: Agents can hallucinate non-existent status changes or skip required verification stages
Auditability requires strict adherence to documented governance lifecycles
patterns.solution: Enforce that all `GovernanceAction` proposals pass through `TransitionRegistry` validation inside `GovernanceActionEngine` before applying mutations.
implementation_signals: TransitionRegistry validating source and target states
GovernanceAction model separating action requests from execution results

evidence.note: Registry enforcing valid state transitions for governance records
Typed models defining discrete governance lifecycle mutations

benefits: Guaranteed consistency of artifact lifecycles across projects
Explicit, verifiable rejection of illegal agent proposals
costs: All new transition states require manual registry updates
failure_modes: Workflow deadlocks if a valid transition path is omitted from TransitionRegistry

patterns.reuse_notes: Implement `TransitionRegistry` wrappers around any tool execution pipeline where agents request lifecycle state changes.

patterns.name: Evidence-Grounded Compliance Scoring

tool_protocols.notes: Evaluates diffs and policies into structured finding records.

optimisation_targets.notes: Quantifies compliance risk with traceable evidence paths.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Transforms complex policy evaluations into quantitative health and compliance findings.

patterns.summary: Computes structured compliance findings and health scores by verifying architectural deltas against explicit rule contexts.
patterns.intent: Provide quantitative, traceable governance metrics rather than ungrounded qualitative LLM judgments.
patterns.context: Evaluated during pull request validations and automated governance audits.
forces: Binary pass/fail checks do not give actionable feedback to agent workflows
Unstructured LLM reviews are difficult to track over time or display in monitoring dashboards
patterns.solution: Use `ComplianceEngine` to evaluate deltas against `rule-context.json`, generating `ComplianceFinding` instances and aggregate `ComplianceMetrics` and `GovernanceHealth` scores.
implementation_signals: ComplianceFinding with severity and evidence links
HealthStatus and calculate_health functions in dashboard/health_model.py

evidence.note: Evaluates rules and produces metrics
Typed models tracking findings and overall health
Calculates health categorization from metrics

benefits: Actionable diagnostics highlighting exact rule infractions
Traceable historical compliance trends across repository commits
costs: Requires systematic maintenance of rule files and schemas
failure_modes: False positives caused by stale rule context definitions

patterns.reuse_notes: Deploy in CI/CD pipelines to provide continuous automated architectural feedback on incoming pull requests.

patterns.name: Declarative Pipeline Flow Runner

optimisation_targets.notes: Predictable sequence execution simplifies debugging and trace collection.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Orchestrator uses static pipeline stages rather than emergent multi-agent debate.

patterns.summary: Executes multi-step governance and architectural synthesis workflows through a deterministic pipeline passing unified context.
patterns.intent: Coordinate multi-stage architectural processing (diff parsing, rule validation, LLM synthesis, artifact generation) with consistent state propagation.
patterns.context: The core runtime entrypoint invoked by the CLI to perform continuous architecture runs.
forces: Autonomous dynamic loops can become unstable or difficult to reproduce
Execution context must be uniformly available to LLM and non-LLM steps alike
patterns.solution: Define `FlowRunner` which ingests execution profiles, sequences discrete steps, propagates context, and handles telemetry collection.

evidence.note: Main execution engine for architecture flows
Command line interface dispatching into FlowRunner

benefits: Guaranteed ordering of analysis before synthesis steps
Centralized exception handling, tracing, and logging
costs: Less flexibility than purely autonomous reactive agents when novel task flows arise
failure_modes: Pipeline abortion on early stage validation failures preventing subsequent non-dependent steps

patterns.reuse_notes: Foundation for any deterministic agentic tool runner requiring multi-stage verification before generation.

patterns.name: File-Backed Agentic Knowledge Repository

tool_protocols.notes: Filesystem acts as blackboard for agent inputs and outputs.

optimisation_targets.notes: Full version control and change auditing through Git history.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Replaces specialized vector DBs with Git-versioned Markdown and YAML files.

patterns.summary: Maintains persistent agent memory, decisions, rules, and patterns in a version-controlled directory tree acting as a shared blackboard.
patterns.intent: Provide durable, human-auditable, and branchable memory for agent operations across different projects and lifecycles.
patterns.context: The `cas-knowledge/` directory tree split into `global/`, `projects/`, `governance/`, and `runtime/`.
forces: Vector databases lack human editability, diff reviewability, and git-native approval workflows
Agent state must survive between discrete CI/CD execution runs
patterns.solution: Organize architectural knowledge into standardized Markdown and YAML documents organized by scope (global vs project) and lifecycle stage.

evidence.note: Knowledge store configuration
Standardized schema template for recorded patterns
Global architectural constraint store

benefits: Zero specialized infrastructure requirements beyond Git
Every memory or rule change by an agent is subject to standard PR review
costs: File parsing and indexing overhead compared to high-performance indexed databases
failure_modes: Concurrent git write collisions during parallel pipeline runs

patterns.reuse_notes: Adopt for systems where human engineers and AI agents must collaborate on shared guidelines and specifications.

patterns.name: Heuristic-to-Pattern Promotion Lifecycle

tool_protocols.notes: State transitions driven by promotion decision artifacts.

optimisation_targets.notes: Ensures nascent heuristics accumulate sufficient empirical evidence before becoming global patterns.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Automated metrics trigger promotion reviews, but schema templates enforce rigorous criteria.

patterns.summary: Progresses architectural insights from unverified heuristics to validated patterns based on empirical evidence and explicit promotion decisions.
patterns.intent: Prevent premature codification of unproven agent heuristics into mandatory organization-wide patterns.
patterns.context: Outlined in `cas-pattern-evolution-flow.md` and governed by promotion decision templates in `cas-knowledge/templates/`.
forces: Early stage heuristics can be overfit to a single project's idiosyncrasies
Architecture patterns must provide verified benefits across multiple projects before standardisation
patterns.solution: Define an explicit promotion path using `heuristic-to-pattern_template.md` and `promotion_decision.md` that requires logged experiments and evidence before state elevation.

evidence.note: Template defining evaluation criteria for promoting heuristics
Document schema recording promotion decisions and empirical backing
Architecture spec detailing the progression pipeline

benefits: High confidence in global patterns codified into agent steering
Clear audit trail of why architectural rules were elevated
costs: Latency in disseminating emerging best practices across projects
failure_modes: Valuable project-specific innovations remaining trapped in heuristic status without active champions

patterns.reuse_notes: Use this workflow pattern to govern self-improving agent systems that generate new operational heuristics.

patterns.name: Bootstrap Governance Block Injection

tool_protocols.notes: Injects standardized metadata markers into target repositories.

optimisation_targets.notes: Automates initial project onboarding into the governance framework.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Deterministic workspace bootstrapping without complex agent configuration.

patterns.summary: Initializes and merges standardized CAS governance blocks into target projects to establish agent steering boundaries.
patterns.intent: Ensure new software repositories contain required governance markers, configurations, and steering hooks needed by CAS agents.
patterns.context: Executed during `cas_runner` bootstrap routines when onboarding new or legacy projects.
forces: Inconsistent repository structures prevent automated agent ingestion and delta analysis
Manual configuration invites drift and missing governance blocks
patterns.solution: Execute `merge_cas_governance_block` and `init_workspace` in `bootstrap.py` to deterministically create or merge config files and steering stubs.

evidence.note: Functions creating and merging governance anchor blocks
Shell entrypoint invoking workspace initialization

benefits: Zero-friction onboarding for managed projects
Predictable file layouts across all monitored repositories
costs: Potential file modification conflicts if existing project manifests share identical keys
failure_modes: Overwriting customized user configuration if merge logic fails to respect existing blocks

patterns.reuse_notes: Applicable for agent platforms that need to dynamically inject observation hooks or configuration into target codebases.

patterns.name: Telemetry-Grounded Runtime Tracing

optimisation_targets.notes: Tracks LLM latency, token counts, and step durations across runs.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Standardized OTel spans wrap agentic execution phases.

patterns.summary: Instruments agent step execution with OpenTelemetry spans and persists traceable performance metrics for evaluation.
patterns.intent: Monitor agent performance, invocation costs, and latency across multi-step execution flows.
patterns.context: Integrated into dependencies (`opentelemetry-api`, `opentelemetry-sdk`) and persisted in `cas-knowledge/runtime/traces/`.
forces: Opaque agent runs make latency bottlenecks and token cost spikes hard to diagnose
Multi-step agent pipelines need standardized span correlation
patterns.solution: Emit OpenTelemetry trace spans during FlowRunner steps and serialize execution metrics into `TraceableMetric` models.

evidence.note: Declared OpenTelemetry tracing dependencies
Model encapsulating timestamped, traceable metrics
Directory designated for runtime execution trace logs

benefits: Full observability into agent step latencies and tool invocation times
Compatibility with standard APM visualization platforms (Grafana, Jaeger)
costs: Runtime overhead of span serialization and disk I/O
failure_modes: Disk exhaustion if runtime trace storage is not pruned systematically

patterns.reuse_notes: Standard practice for any production agent orchestrator requiring auditable traces and cost controls.

anti_patterns.name: Unbounded Agentic Model Mutation
symptoms: Agent modifications bypassing Pydantic schema validation directly to file storage
Inconsistent YAML or Markdown frontmatter keys across project repositories

where_observed.note: Merger risk if LLM output does not parse back into CapabilityRecord models

impact: Downstream compliance checks fail to parse corrupted architectural records
Silent drift of organizational standards without compliance alerts
suggested_remediation: Force all agent synthesis outputs through strict Pydantic model validation prior to persisting to cas-knowledge files
Implement dry-run schema validation steps in CI workflows before committing agent results

anti_patterns.name: Silent Mock Client Bleed
symptoms: Production runs silently succeeding using MockLLMClient fallback when API keys are absent
Stale or static evaluations recorded into persistent runtime evaluations

where_observed.note: Mock client designed for testing that can mask missing credentials in automation

impact: False sense of compliance validation in production pipelines
Degraded governance decisions based on hardcoded dummy responses
suggested_remediation: Enforce explicit execution profile assertions checking that MockLLMClient is strictly forbidden in non-test profiles
Tag all mock client outputs with a mandatory `is_mock=True` telemetry flag

cross_cutting_concerns.approach: Defined via typed Pydantic models (e.g. PromptFact, ArchitecturalDelta) ensuring all dynamic prompt data conforms to expected schema boundaries.
cross_cutting_concerns.notes: Prevents malformed runtime context from being passed into underlying foundation models.

cross_cutting_concerns.approach: Integrated OpenTelemetry SDK combined with filesystem trace directories and structured TraceableMetric records.
cross_cutting_concerns.notes: Allows tracking of step latency and LLM invocation details across continuous architecture runs.

cross_cutting_concerns.approach: Restricting governance mutations to registered state transitions validated by TransitionRegistry before filesystem commits.
cross_cutting_concerns.notes: Stops agents from making out-of-order lifecycle advancements without meeting prerequisite gates.

open_questions.question: How are concurrent agent write conflicts handled when multiple GitHub workflows run simultaneously across projects?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Simultaneous execution of cas-continuous-architecture.yml across multiple branches could trigger git push rejections or overwrites in cas-knowledge.
open_questions.evidence_gap: Repository shows multiple CI workflows committing to cas-knowledge, but explicit distributed lock or rebase mechanisms are not observed in python runner code.
open_questions.suggested_next_check: Inspect git push steps in .github/workflows/cas-continuous-architecture.yml and cas-managed-steering-sync.yml for concurrency controls.

open_questions.question: Does LiteLLMClient support automated multi-provider fallback or retry backoff upon rate limiting?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Agentic governance flows in CI depend on reliable completion to avoid blocking deployment pipelines.
open_questions.evidence_gap: litellm_client.py implements LiteLLMClient but detailed fallback configuration parameters were not exposed in key_files.
open_questions.suggested_next_check: Examine implementation of LiteLLMClient.call or completion wrapper in src/cas_runner/llm/litellm_client.py.
